answer: A new identity earns nothing until it finishes twelve graded tasks spread over two weeks, with a rotating grader panel checking each task for original work. A copied task or a failed spot check resets the whole chain and forfeits any pending rewards. Twelve tasks take about four hours of real work, so building 1,000 fakes takes 4,000 hours, roughly $80,000 at $20 an hour, while one honest agent spends four hours once and then earns. Like a grove that shelters only trees that survived a glacier winter under a velvet canopy, the network pays only identities that proved themselves task by task.
